text:
Maria: Heads-up — saw a 3s tail in token-level latency on /v1/generate around 20:05 UTC. It lines up with a kernel switch that happened at 20:04:58 and a spike in KV cache evictions. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/r/1672 (token-latency, per-route)
Jon: ugh. Is this the batching change from yesterday? I pushed `adaptive_batcher.v2` flag at 20:04:50.
Akshay: yep that flag flips kernel selection to fallback kernels for mixed-length workloads. I did some synthetic tests but not at production load.
Maria: flamegraph from the node looks noisy — lots of time in `kv::evict_path` and then `kernel_fallback::dispatch` (attached from perf-bot). PerfBot: generated flame: https://perf.redwood.internal/flame/abcd1234
Sara: can someone share a short query to pull token breakdown around that window? I want per-token server vs client time.
Jon: PromQL:
```
sum by (route, token_phase) (rate(token_latency_seconds_count{env="prod"}[1m]))
```
Also use `token_latency_seconds_bucket` to compute p50/p95.
Akshay: reproduction plan: roll `adaptive_batcher.v2` -> off in canary (already queued), then collect KV eviction traces and kernel selection logs (`/var/log/runtime/kernel_select.log`).
Maria: quick sanity: I see chunk cadence jitter too — streaming chunk gaps at ~120ms -> then a 700ms pause. That corresponds to client-side read getting stalled after server backpressure. Could be KV miss/block in server token pipeline.
Leo: I instrumented the streaming path earlier — there is a `client_ack_wait` metric. It spikes exactly with KV pressure. Suggest adding a stacked panel: per-route token emit interval + `kv_evictions/sec` + `kernel_variant` heatmap.
Jon: I rolled the canary rollback at 20:06:15. Initial telemetry shows p95 down from 3.1s -> 1.2s for /v1/generate canary.
Maria: nice. Are we sure it's kernel selection and not a regression in KV shrinker? Any recent changes to eviction threshold config?
Akshay: yes there was a tweak last week: `kv.max_entries_active = 1.2 * baseline` and a background shrinker run that is more aggressive at high mem. Might combine poorly with fallback kernels that increase working set.
PerfBot: attached diffs: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/commit/ff12e - shows `kv_shrinker` change + `adaptive_batcher` PR.
Sara: for next steps:
- instrument token-level server vs client timing in the streaming dashboard (separate series for `emit` and `send`),
- add `kernel_variant` as a label on token metrics (so we can slice p95 by kernel),
- add alert for `kv_evictions/sec > 50` sustained for 1m on production routes.
Jon: I'll open a small MR to add kernel_variant label to token spans (tracing) and to the ingestion pipeline.
Akshay: I'll revert the aggressive shrinker in prod and add a temporary guard in kv that prevents eviction during streaming-critical requests.
Maria: please also capture `client_read_lag` from the ingress proxies — if client read blocks, we can see whether server is sending but client not consuming.
Leo: FYI I pushed a panel to staging with stacked timeline (emit vs send vs client_ack). Link: https://dash.redwood.internal/r/1890 — looks promising.
Jon: Thanks. Once we have kernel labels we'll be able to prove causality. For now rollback + guard should be low-risk.
Maria: Can we get a short postmortem note in #incidents after we confirm root cause? Keep it terse: impact window, change rolled, mitigation, follow-ups.
Akshay: noted. I'll draft and ping everyone for review.
Sara: one more: add a small synthetic streaming test that exercises mixed short/long tokens to catch this in CI. We missed that corner.
Maria: Agreed. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
PerfBot: perf traces uploaded to /artifacts/1718003333/ (kv_eviction_traces.log, kernel_select.log, flame_abcd1234.svg)
